research_question: Can explicit one-token EOS supervision restore proper answer termination and reduce free-generation repetition while preserving held-out reference-continuation learning?
only_changed_training_variable: one canonical <eos> id=3 supervised immediately after each unchanged chosen answer

controls.canonical_parent: same SHA256 verified canonical v14a2 full state, fresh strict load per arm
controls.tokenizer: tokenizer_v9 with 52224 vocabulary and exactly mapped EOS=3 EOT=7
controls.data: same 28 authored gradient_clipping training rows, four per semantic family, unchanged chosen text and holdout of 32 rows
controls.sampler: v14a6 TargetPulseSampler(seed=928+801), same sampled row IDs order across arms
controls.optimizer: fresh AdamW all trainable weights per arm, weight_decay=0
controls.reference_ce: original 28 chosen tokens NLL with no EOS for both arms
controls.reference_heldout_nll: original 32 chosen answers teacher-forced excluding EOS for both arms
controls.generation: same historical greedy argmax EOS/EOT stop and evaluation

metrics: first-sentence keyword rubric success (not human judgment)
EOS and EOT probability after full reference answer
full-generation trigram repetition rate and high-repetition count

predeclared_decision.eos_probability_restored: u40 mean EOS+EOT p >= 0.1 on 32 holdout reference endings
predeclared_decision.repetition_reduced: u40 high-repetition count falls by >= 8 of 32 AND mean trigram repetition rate falls
predeclared_decision.heldout_reference_learning_preserved: u40 heldout reference NLL regression <= 0.1 AND heldout top1 regression <= 0.02
predeclared_decision.promotion: No promotion regardless of decision; this is a one-seed one-route ablation.

limitation: Adding one EOS label per example changes total CE normalization slightly, inseparable from this supervision change. Teacher-forced end-token probability alone does not prove natural answer stopping.
